info.title: Meerkat Data Plane
info.description:
What Meerkat serves on the data plane besides your routes: sign-in and profile pages, the account button and portal bar, the live channel, developer tools and, in the Enterprise edition, the OpenID provider and notifications. Developers read your routes' APIs at /meerkat/apidocs.

Browsers are identified by the session cookie set at sign-in, programs by a personal API token (`Authorization: Bearer mk_...`, from /profile/tokens). Pages answer HTML and redirect (303) to sign-in when needed. A POST from another site's page is refused (403). Page form submissions are not listed.

get.description: WebSocket (RFC 6455, version 13, HTTP/1.1), server to page only: each text frame is one `LiveMessage`. Every page gets `served` and `unserved`; signed-in pages also their account's messages; developers also developer messages. A notification message carries only its id and change: read the rest through the API. Same origin only.

The other readers' pages update at once.

get.description: Enterprise edition. The service worker the account button registers to show a notification on the desktop with its buttons: open the detail, run an action. It controls no page and intercepts no request.

Authorization code flow with PKCE, no consent screen. The first route of the client whose rule admits the person decides the claims. Errors before the client and redirect are verified show a page; after, they go back to the application.

session.name: MEERKAT_SESSION
session.description: Session cookie set at sign-in (`__Host-MEERKAT_SESSION` over HTTPS, with an optional installation suffix). HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax.

apiToken.description: Personal API token (`mk_...`) from /profile/tokens. Acts as its owner in its tenant and group. Refused on the admin port.

oidcAccessToken.description: An access token from the OpenID provider.

next.name: next
next.description: Path of this site to land on (anything else lands on `/`)

challenge.description: Single-use challenge id, for the finish call's `challenge`
Single-use challenge id, for the finish call's `challenge`

PasskeyAttestation.description: PublicKeyCredential with an attestation response, base64url

PasskeyAssertion.description: PublicKeyCredential with an assertion response, base64url

total.description: Unread notifications the reader can open, all their tenants

page.description: The notifications page for this reader: the portal's page when they may open its route, else `/meerkat/notifications`

inBar.description: The portal bar carries the notifications entry and the badge; the account button then shows neither

ServedName.description: A service served from a developer's machine

who.description: Who serves it; absent for a program

authenticated.description: Signed in; false fills display fields only

initials.description: Shown when there is no photo

tenants.description: Tenants to switch to, when several

apps.description: Applications the session may open, when several

roles.description: Role names set as classes on `<body>`

schemeImposed.description: Scheme imposed by the route: no switch

labels.description: Menu strings by key, in the visitor's language

icon.description: SVG drawn as a mask; else the label's initial

href.description: Link; a container's first enabled module

badge.description: Unread notifications, on the notifications entry and the container holding it

route.description: Route id; `notifications` for the notifications entry

layout.description: header: parents on top, children in a rail; rail: the reverse

screenshot.description: png, jpeg or webp base64 data URI, under about 1.5 MiB

data.description: A served service for served and unserved; `{id, change}` for notifications; anything for an echo

groupMode.description: Group mode; empty without a tenant

users.description: Every user, with their groups here

roles.description: Role names; those not valid as a CSS class are dropped

read.description: The same in every tenant it reached the reader in

actions.description: Actions the reader may use; a route link carries `notification=<id>`. Call `url` with `method`, and `body` as JSON when present

body.description: JSON value to send, with `Content-Type: application/json`

tenant.description: The tenant it was sent in; for a message sent to several of the reader's tenants, the current one when it reached them there

here.description: Sent in the current tenant. False: open it and run its actions from its own tenant

tenants.description: Every tenant it reached the reader in: one, or several for a message sent to all of them

group.description: A message sent to several tenants: the same for every copy, reader and session

ids.description: With `group`: the ids of every copy the reader holds; any of them reads or deletes this item

ack.description: It asks to be acknowledged: `single`, the first reader closes it for everyone; `all`, each reader. Absent when it asks for none.

acknowledged.description: With `ack`, once done for you: when, and who when somebody else closed it (single). Absent while you owe it: then it cannot be deleted.

by.description: Who closed it, when it was not you

state.description: Its sender withdrew it: show a placeholder saying so. The item then carries nothing of what it said (no level, title, text, sender, link, action or tenant), is read, and asks for nothing. A replaced notification is not listed: its replacement stands in its place.

exercise.description: Sent to practise: show it labelled EXERCISE (translated as the page's other strings).

NotificationTenantCount.description: A tenant the reader holds notifications in

total.description: Notifications held there, a message sent to several tenants counted in each

more.description: More pages: ask again with `before` the last `createdAt`

tenants.description: First page only (no `before`): every tenant the reader holds notifications in, by name, whatever `tenant` asked. Offer a filter when there are two or more

unread.description: First page only: unread over all the reader's tenants, a message sent to several of them counted once

access_token.description: Signed JWT: the route's claims and sub, iss, aud, client_id, scope, iat, exp, jti

id_token.description: Signed JWT (RS256): the route's claims and sub, iss, aud, azp, iat, exp, nonce, auth_time

refresh_token.description: Valid once; ends with the user's Meerkat session
